# Building from Source

This page covers the prerequisites and commands for building Mayon from source.

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Version | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Node.js | 22 | Set via `.nvmrc`. Use `nvm install && nvm use`. |
| pnpm | 10 | Set in `packageManager`. Enable with `corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@10 --activate`. |
| Docker | — | Required to run Postgres and the Mayon server. |

No bun.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `pnpm install` | Install Node.js dependencies. |
| `pnpm dev` | Bring up the all-Docker dev stack (web HMR at http://localhost:5173 + server + Postgres), project `mayon-dev`. |
| `pnpm dev:build` | Rebuild the dev images (after deps, config, or `@mayon/shared` changes). |
| `docker compose up` | Run the full stack: web SPA + server + Postgres (web on :8080). |
| `pnpm build` | Build the SPA into `build/`. |
| `pnpm check` | Type-check with `svelte-check`. |
| `pnpm lint` | ESLint (flat config) + Prettier `--check`. |
| `pnpm format` | Prettier `--write`. |
| `pnpm test` | Tiers 1+2 (Node + Chromium), capability-gated — the local merge gate. |
| `pnpm test:unit` | Tier 1: in-process logic, repositories, and server handlers. |
| `pnpm test:browser` | Tier 2: real-Chromium component tests. |
| `pnpm test:e2e` | Tier 3: Playwright against a running stack. |
| `pnpm test:low-spec` | Serial mode for low-spec machines; still selects every test. |
| `pnpm test:watch` | Vitest in watch mode (Tiers 1+2). |
| `pnpm check:tests` | Tier guardrails (`TT-001`–`TT-008`). |
| `pnpm --filter @mayon/server test` | Vitest for the server package. |
| `pnpm db:generate` | Generate a new drizzle migration from `src/lib/db/schema.ts` into `drizzle/`. |
| `pnpm db:studio` | Open Drizzle Studio against the schema. |

## Development workflow

The typical inner-loop runs the entire stack (web + server + Postgres) in Docker:

```bash
pnpm dev   # web HMR on http://localhost:5173, server on :4319, Postgres
```

Web (`.svelte`, `.ts`, CSS) changes are reflected instantly via HMR; the Vite
container proxies `/api` requests to the Dockerized server. Rebuild the images
after dependency, config, or `@mayon/shared` changes with `pnpm dev:build`.

For the full stack from prebuilt images:

```bash
docker compose up   # web on :8080, server + Postgres in containers
```

## Testing

Tests are split into three enforced tiers. Place a test at the lowest tier that can
prove its claim:

1. Pure logic, mappers, repositories, or server handlers → **Tier 1**:
   colocated `*.test.ts`, run in Node with `pnpm test:unit`.
2. Rendered markup, clicks/keys/focus, responsive state, or Svelte reactivity →
   **Tier 2**: colocated `*.browser.test.ts`, run in real Chromium with
   `pnpm test:browser`.
3. Real streaming, persistence, multi-page navigation, hydration, or auth/setup →
   **Tier 3**: `tests/e2e/*.spec.ts`, run with `pnpm test:e2e` against a running
   stack.

If two tiers can prove the same claim, keep the lower-tier test and delete the
higher-tier copy. `pnpm test` runs Tiers 1+2. `*.svelte.test.ts` remains a
rune-module test in Tier 1; Tier 2 uses the `*.browser.test.ts` suffix.

On a fresh checkout, build the shared package once first (its compiled output is
required by tests and is not produced by `pnpm install`):

```bash
pnpm --filter @mayon/shared build
```

Component tests supply `$app/*` and store dependencies at the module boundary and
mock `fetch` with MSW; shared handlers live in `tests/mocks/handlers.ts`, and the
worker asset under `tests/mocks/public/` is served only by the test Vite server —
it never enters `build/`. Tier 2 must not need the application server, Postgres,
or docker compose.

Tier 3 keeps only flows that need the real browser, server, and persistence. It
reuses captured session state (`tests/e2e/global-setup.ts`), never replays
onboarding per test, and uses condition-based assertions instead of fixed waits.
Before keeping an end-to-end case, check whether Tier 1 or Tier 2 can prove it;
remove the duplicate and record the replacement or retirement rationale in
`specs/032-test-suite-tiering/migration-ledger.md`. Every removed or migrated
source-text and end-to-end case needs a ledger row.

The capability gate parallelizes only at ≥8 logical CPUs and ≥8 GiB usable RAM;
low-spec or unreadable machines run serially. On a low-spec machine use
`pnpm test:low-spec` (it sets `MAYON_TEST_PARALLEL=off` and a 500 MB V8 heap);
`MAYON_TEST_MAX_WORKERS` caps a capable machine. The gate changes concurrency,
never test selection. `pnpm check:tests` enforces the tier boundaries and CI
enforces per-tier budgets from `test-budgets.json` via `pnpm check:budget`.

## Browser E2E tests

The chat experience has Playwright E2E coverage (`tests/e2e/`), deliberately limited to
flows that need the real browser, server, and persistence: provider onboarding through the
real Settings UI plus a full send → receive round trip, streamed markdown/mermaid/selection
rendering, quiz and lab generation, branch back-propagation, and image parts. Lower-tier
logic and component tests own everything else; every removed case is recorded in
`specs/032-test-suite-tiering/migration-ledger.md`. The reply comes from a tests-owned mock
LLM service (`mock-llm` in `docker-compose.dev.yml`) that speaks the OpenAI chat protocol —
no real AI service, no API key, no external network. The suite runs automatically in the
`e2e` CI job on every pull request.

Since feature 020 the mock also discriminates request kinds — chat, quiz generation, lab generation,
short-answer grading, and learning-brief generation — and answers each with its own deterministic
fixture (short-answer grading is steered by an answer-text lever: answers containing "should be
correct" grade correct, "should be wrong" grade incorrect). The classification protocol,
fixtures, and the no-interception guardrail are specified in `tests/fixtures/mock-llm/README.md`
and `../history/appendices/020-mock-llm-protocol.md` — never stub the provider request path
with `page.route`; a bypassed hop tests the mocks, not the app.

Prerequisites (fresh checkout):

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm --filter @mayon/shared build
pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium
```

Run against a running dev stack:

```bash
pnpm dev:up
pnpm test:e2e
```

The suite needs the stack up because the provider request path executes inside the `server`
container; the mock is reachable only there. Failed runs leave traces in `test-results/` and a
browser-runnable report in `playwright-report/` (open with `pnpm exec playwright show-report`).

If your `mayon-dev` stack is busy serving a different checkout (the bind mounts follow whoever ran
`pnpm dev:up` last), run the suite against an isolated stack for this checkout instead — the volumes
and network are project-prefixed, so nothing collides. Note that the `mock-llm` service mounts its
fixture directory read-only, so after editing anything under `tests/fixtures/mock-llm/` restart it
(`docker compose -p <project> restart mock-llm`):

```bash
docker compose -p mayon-e2e -f docker-compose.dev.yml -f docker-compose.e2e.yml up -d
E2E_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5174 pnpm test:e2e
docker compose -p mayon-e2e -f docker-compose.dev.yml -f docker-compose.e2e.yml down
```

### Sharded runs

The suite can be split across concurrently running Playwright shards (this is
how the `e2e` CI job runs — one shard job each with its own stack). Each shard
gets its own compose project (`mayon-dev-shard-N`, web on host port `5200+N`,
volumes/network isolated by the project prefix), so there are no shared-state
races between shards:

```bash
pnpm dev:shard:up 1/4    # boot shard-1's stack + readiness waits
pnpm dev:shard:test 1/4  # playwright --shard=1/4 against that stack
pnpm dev:shard:down 1    # tear the stack down
```

CI runs four shards; run them in separate terminals to divide the wall time. The
shard override file uses the compose merge tag `!override` for its port lists,
which requires Docker Compose v2.24 or newer. The capability gate decides each
runner's worker count, and sharding only distributes work across runners that
individually meet the threshold.
